findings.title: Rejected devices are cached and then allowed on the next request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache with SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, and it never evicts that entry when the store returns an error. A new device over the limit therefore fails once with ErrDeviceLimitReached, but its next request on the same instance within the 29-minute cache TTL hits the early cache return, TagDevice reports success, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants an identity even though the device was never inserted. Concurrent requests can also observe the cache entry set by an in-flight request that is later rejected. Set the cache only after a successful store write, or delete the entry on error.

findings.title: Device-limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices in one database session and then performs the insert/upsert in a separate session, with no transaction, lock, or database constraint enforcing the maximum row count. Two concurrent requests for different new devices, on the same or different Grafana instances, can both observe count == deviceLimit-1 and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. The per-process local cache does not coordinate distinct device IDs or multiple instances. The count check and admission of a new device need to be made atomic, for example with a locking transaction or another database-enforced mechanism.

findings.title: Provider signature changes are not reflected in dependency wiring
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changes its third parameter from anonstore.AnonStore to db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore in anonstore/database.go additionally changes from accepting only db.DB to requiring an int64 deviceLimit. The checked-in Wire injector/provider wiring that calls these constructors is not updated or regenerated in this PR, so code generated/called with the old arguments no longer compiles and Wire has no ordinary injectable int64 binding for the new store parameter. Update and regenerate the wiring, or keep the store injectable and supply the configured limit through its existing provider wiring.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now blocks on device tagging without a timeout
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged devices in a goroutine with panic recovery and a two-minute background-context timeout. It now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context and no timeout or recovery. A slow or blocked anon_device count/insert therefore stalls anonymous authentication for the full database/request duration, request cancellation can abort the limit decision, and a panic in tagging now propagates into request authentication instead of merely degrading tagging. Use a bounded context for the now-synchronous enforcement call and preserve appropriate panic handling.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is absent from shipped configuration definitions
findings.body: The PR parses auth.anonymous/device_limit into Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, but it does not add device_limit to conf/defaults.ini, the sample configuration, or the Grafana configuration documentation. Operators therefore cannot discover the new limit from the shipped configuration, and configuration/environment handling that enumerates known keys may not surface it consistently. Add the default and explanatory documentation alongside the existing auth.anonymous settings.

findings.title: Device-limit tests do not cover allowed updates or the service authentication path
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second distinct device is rejected by the store when the limit is 1. It does not verify the intended complementary behavior that the already-admitted device can still be updated while count >= limit, and no test exercises AnonDeviceService.TagDevice or Anonymous.Authenticate repeatedly after a rejection. Those missing cases leave both the updateDevice success path and service-level enforcement behaviour unverified. Add tests for updating the existing device at the limit and for repeated service-level requests from a rejected device.
